title: Pride and Prejudice
author: Jane Austen
description: Elizabeth Bennet and the proud Mr Darcy misjudge each other at every turn in a comedy of manners about marriage, money and the English gentry.

title: Nineteen Eighty-Four
author: George Orwell
description: Winston Smith rewrites history for the Party by day and dreams of rebellion by night, until the Thought Police catch up with him. Orwell's portrait of total surveillance has never gone out of date.

title: Animal Farm
author: George Orwell
description: The animals of Manor Farm drive out their farmer and set up a society of equals, which the pigs quietly turn into something much worse. A short, sharp fable about revolutions that eat themselves.

title: The Great Gatsby
author: F. Scott Fitzgerald
description: Nick Carraway spends a summer next door to Jay Gatsby, a mysterious millionaire throwing parties for a woman across the bay. A compact novel about longing and the price of reinvention.

title: To Kill a Mockingbird
author: Harper Lee
description: Scout Finch watches her father defend a Black man falsely accused of a crime in a small Alabama town. Childhood, conscience and prejudice seen through a sharp young narrator.

title: Moby-Dick
author: Herman Melville
description: Ishmael signs on to a whaling ship whose captain is hunting one particular white whale. Part adventure, part encyclopedia of whaling, part meditation on obsession.

title: Jane Eyre
author: Charlotte Brontë
description: An orphan governess with a fierce sense of her own worth takes a post at Thornfield Hall and falls for its brooding master, who is keeping a secret upstairs.

title: Wuthering Heights
author: Emily Brontë
description: Heathcliff and Catherine's destructive passion plays out across two generations on the Yorkshire moors. Wild, strange and unlike any other Victorian novel.

title: Crime and Punishment
author: Fyodor Dostoevsky
description: A poor student in St Petersburg convinces himself that an extraordinary man may commit murder for a greater good, then discovers what guilt actually feels like.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
author: Fyodor Dostoevsky
description: Three brothers, a dissolute father and a murder: Dostoevsky's last novel argues about God, freedom and responsibility through people who are impossible to forget.

title: War and Peace
author: Leo Tolstoy
description: Five aristocratic families live through Napoleon's invasion of Russia. Balls, battles, love affairs and Tolstoy's own theory of history, in the Pevear and Volokhonsky translation.

title: Anna Karenina
author: Leo Tolstoy
description: A married woman in Petersburg society falls for a cavalry officer while, in parallel, a landowner tries to work out how to live well. Tolstoy's most perfectly built novel.

title: Adventures of Huckleberry Finn
author: Mark Twain
description: Huck fakes his own death and floats down the Mississippi on a raft with Jim, a man escaping slavery. Funny, troubling and the root of a great deal of American writing.

title: The Picture of Dorian Gray
author: Oscar Wilde
description: A beautiful young man wishes that his portrait would age instead of him, and gets his wish. Wilde's only novel, glittering with epigrams and quietly horrifying.

title: A Tale of Two Cities
author: Charles Dickens
description: London and Paris during the Terror, a dissolute lawyer who looks exactly like a French aristocrat, and one of the most famous closing lines in English fiction.

title: Great Expectations
author: Charles Dickens
description: Pip, a blacksmith's boy, is raised to be a gentleman by an anonymous benefactor and learns that expectations are a poor substitute for character.

title: Frankenstein
author: Mary Shelley
description: Victor Frankenstein assembles a living being and abandons it in disgust; the creature, articulate and alone, comes looking for him. Arguably the first science fiction novel.

title: Dune
author: Frank Herbert
description: Young Paul Atreides is thrust into a war for the desert planet Arrakis, the only source of the spice that makes interstellar travel possible. Ecology, religion and dynastic intrigue on a vast scale.

title: Foundation
author: Isaac Asimov
description: A mathematician predicts the fall of the Galactic Empire and sets up a colony of scholars to shorten the dark age that follows. The first of Asimov's long game of history as science.

title: The Left Hand of Darkness
author: Ursula K. Le Guin
description: An envoy from a league of worlds arrives on a frozen planet whose people have no fixed sex. A political thriller that is also a patient study of friendship across difference.

title: Neuromancer
author: William Gibson
description: A washed-up console cowboy is hired for one last run against an artificial intelligence. The book that gave us cyberspace, written before most people had seen a modem.

title: Fahrenheit 451
author: Ray Bradbury
description: Guy Montag is a fireman whose job is to burn books, until a curious neighbour makes him wonder what is in them. A short novel about screens, distraction and the cost of forgetting.

title: Brave New World
author: Aldous Huxley
description: In a World State where citizens are engineered, conditioned and kept content with soma, a man raised outside the system is brought in as a curiosity. Orwell's rival vision of the future.

title: The Hitchhiker's Guide to the Galaxy
author: Douglas Adams
description: Seconds before Earth is demolished to make way for a hyperspace bypass, Arthur Dent is rescued by his friend Ford Prefect, who turns out to be an alien. Don't panic.

title: The Hobbit
author: J. R. R. Tolkien
description: Bilbo Baggins, a hobbit who likes his comforts, is talked into joining thirteen dwarves on a journey to steal back their treasure from a dragon. He finds a ring along the way.

title: The Fellowship of the Ring
author: J. R. R. Tolkien
description: Frodo inherits the One Ring and sets out from the Shire with eight companions to destroy it in the fire where it was made. The first volume of The Lord of the Rings.

title: A Wizard of Earthsea
author: Ursula K. Le Guin
description: A gifted young wizard, showing off at school, looses a shadow into the world and must hunt it across the islands of Earthsea. A fantasy about names, pride and balance.

title: Alice's Adventures in Wonderland and Through the Looking-Glass
author: Lewis Carroll
description: Alice follows a white rabbit down a hole and later steps through a mirror, meeting caterpillars, queens and chess pieces who argue with impeccable illogic. Both Alice books in one volume.

title: Dracula
author: Bram Stoker
description: Told through letters, diaries and newspaper cuttings, the story of a Transylvanian count's move to England and the small group who work out what he is. The vampire novel all others answer to.

title: The Hound of the Baskervilles
author: Arthur Conan Doyle
description: A family curse, a spectral hound on the moor and a new heir at Baskerville Hall. Holmes sends Watson to Devon ahead of him in the best-loved of the long Sherlock Holmes stories.

title: The Adventures of Sherlock Holmes
author: Arthur Conan Doyle
description: Twelve cases from Baker Street, including A Scandal in Bohemia, The Red-Headed League and The Speckled Band. The stories that made the detective story a popular form.

title: The Murder of Roger Ackroyd
author: Agatha Christie
description: Hercule Poirot has retired to grow vegetable marrows in a quiet village when a wealthy neighbour is stabbed in his study. The novel whose solution caused a scandal and is still argued about.

title: The Big Sleep
author: Raymond Chandler
description: Private investigator Philip Marlowe is hired by a dying millionaire to deal with a blackmailer and ends up in a tangle of pornographers, gamblers and two very dangerous daughters.

title: The Maltese Falcon
author: Dashiell Hammett
description: Sam Spade's partner is shot on a job for a client who lied about everything, and soon everyone in San Francisco wants a jewelled black bird. Hard-boiled fiction at its leanest.

title: The Histories
author: Herodotus
description: The first work of history in the Western tradition: the wars between Greece and Persia, told with digressions on Egypt, Scythia and anything else Herodotus found interesting.

title: The History of the Peloponnesian War
author: Thucydides
description: An Athenian general's account of the war between Athens and Sparta, written to be useful to anyone who wants to understand how states and people behave under pressure.

title: Guns, Germs, and Steel
author: Jared Diamond
description: Why did Eurasian societies end up conquering others rather than the reverse? Diamond's answer runs through domesticable crops, animals, disease and the shape of continents.

title: Sapiens: A Brief History of Humankind
author: Yuval Noah Harari
description: From the cognitive revolution to the agricultural and scientific ones, a fast tour of how one species of ape came to run the planet, and what the shared fictions that hold us together cost.

title: On the Origin of Species
author: Charles Darwin
description: Darwin lays out, patiently and with a wealth of examples from pigeons to barnacles, the case that species change over time through natural selection.

title: A Brief History of Time
author: Stephen Hawking
description: Black holes, the big bang, the arrow of time and the search for a theory of everything, explained for readers with no physics and, famously, only one equation.

title: Cosmos
author: Carl Sagan
description: The companion to the television series: fifteen billion years of cosmic evolution, the history of science and the case for wonder as a way of looking at the universe.

title: The Selfish Gene
author: Richard Dawkins
description: Evolution seen from the gene's point of view: organisms as survival machines and cooperation as something that selfish replicators can nonetheless produce. Introduced the word meme.

title: Meditations
author: Marcus Aurelius
description: Private notes a Roman emperor wrote to himself on campaign about how to stay decent, calm and useful. Stoicism as practised rather than preached.

title: The Republic
author: Plato
description: Socrates and friends set out to define justice and end up designing a city, with the allegory of the cave, the philosopher-kings and a famous argument for throwing out the poets.

title: Nicomachean Ethics
author: Aristotle
description: What is the good life, and how do you train yourself to live it? Aristotle's answer centres on virtue as a habit, friendship and the practical wisdom to find the mean.

title: The Prince
author: Niccolò Machiavelli
description: A short, unsentimental manual on how rulers gain and keep power, written by a Florentine official hoping for a job. Its name became an adjective for a reason.

title: Thus Spoke Zarathustra
author: Friedrich Nietzsche
description: A prophet comes down from the mountain to teach the overman, the eternal return and the death of God, in a book written as scripture and parody at once.

title: The Odyssey
author: Homer
description: Odysseus takes ten years to get home from Troy past a cyclops, a witch, the sirens and the dead, while his wife holds off a houseful of suitors. Robert Fagles's translation.

title: The Iliad
author: Homer
description: A few weeks in the last year of the Trojan War: Achilles's rage, Hector's duty and the gods meddling from above. Robert Fagles's translation.

title: Paradise Lost
author: John Milton
description: Satan's revolt, the fall of Adam and Eve and the justification of the ways of God to men, in twelve books of blank verse whose villain steals the show.

title: The Complete Poems of Emily Dickinson
author: Emily Dickinson
description: Nearly eighteen hundred short poems, most unpublished in her lifetime, about death, faith, bees and the inside of a mind, with the dashes left as she wrote them.

title: Leaves of Grass
author: Walt Whitman
description: Whitman kept revising and expanding this collection for the rest of his life. Song of Myself and its companions celebrate the body, the crowd and the continent in long unrhymed lines.

title: The Diary of a Young Girl
author: Anne Frank
description: The diary Anne Frank kept for two years while her family hid from the Nazis in an Amsterdam annexe, written by a teenager who wanted to be a writer and became one.

title: Narrative of the Life of Frederick Douglass
author: Frederick Douglass
description: Douglass's own account of growing up enslaved in Maryland, teaching himself to read and escaping north. Short, exact and furious.

title: The Autobiography of Benjamin Franklin
author: Benjamin Franklin
description: Printer, inventor, diplomat and self-improver, Franklin tells his own story up to 1757 with a schedule of virtues he never quite managed to keep.

title: Charlotte's Web
author: E. B. White
description: Wilbur the pig is going to be slaughtered in the autumn, until a spider called Charlotte starts spelling out words in her web. A small book about friendship and mortality.

title: Where the Wild Things Are
author: Maurice Sendak
description: Sent to bed without supper, Max sails to the land of the wild things, becomes their king and comes home to find his dinner still warm.

title: Treasure Island
author: Robert Louis Stevenson
description: Jim Hawkins finds a treasure map in a dead pirate's sea chest and sails off to find it, with a one-legged cook called Long John Silver who is not what he seems.

title: The Secret Garden
author: Frances Hodgson Burnett
description: A sour orphan sent to live with her uncle on the moors finds a walled garden locked for ten years and, in bringing it back to life, brings back a sick cousin and herself.

title: Anne of Green Gables
author: L. M. Montgomery
description: An elderly brother and sister on Prince Edward Island send for an orphan boy to help on the farm and receive a red-haired, talkative girl instead. They keep her.
